﻿M3-T11-184 — Physical product-phase denominator and cubic cofactor tail preflight
CURRENT RESULT
2026-10-02. Current authority was MAIN/INDEX/short RESULT-LEDGER/active ROUTE/latest183. Only needed dependencies and ROUTE §17 were consulted; no restart of historical research.
Adopt: an exact physical product-phase adapter, the fresh identity c_u^sharp=(tau_0^sharp)^3 M_rel, a scoped summed cubic-divisor tail upper bound, and an exponent-budget obstruction for using that bound alone on the present residual. This is not a global closure. PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0. Within-session deductive review; independent hostile audit NOT RUN. TI parked;120 retracted;147–149 frozen.


1. Physical product-phase adapter
Work on primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B and the retained finite nonzero corrected common-u locus. Define x_i=e_i/R>0, y_i=signed opposite-face diagonal/R, w_i=x_i+i y_i=Q/r_i. Then x_i²+y_i²=1 and x_1²+x_2²+x_3²=1. Put Z_ph=w_1 w_2 w_3=X+iY, so X²+Y²=1. Write T=sum_i x_i y_i and S=2T. The corrected133 physical adapter is v_i=2T-4x_i y_i, P=v_1 v_2 v_3, and P/S=4u²/(1+u²).
Two exact identities are
T Y=2x_1 x_2 x_3,
S P=64(x_1 x_2 x_3)².
For the first, expand Y=sum_i y_i x_j x_k-y_1 y_2 y_3. After multiplication by T, the mixed terms cancel because x_i²+x_j²=y_k², and the diagonal terms give x_1x_2x_3 sum_i y_i²=2x_1x_2x_3.
For the second put A_i=x_i y_i, p_i=x_i², sum_i p_i=1. Direct expansion gives T product_i(T-2A_i)=2 sum_{i<j} A_i² A_j²-sum_i A_i^4. Substitution A_i²=p_i(1-p_i) reduces this expression to 4p_1p_2p_3. Since S P=16 T product_i(T-2A_i), the displayed formula follows.
On S!=0 these imply P/S=4Y². Combining with the corrected common-u adapter yields u² X²=Y². On finite nonzero u, X and Y are nonzero; Y also follows from T Y=2x_1x_2x_3>0. Only u=±Y/X is claimed; no unproved sign choice is used.
Write u=a/b reduced, c_u²=a²+b² as in133/183. Since gcd(a,c_u)=gcd(b,c_u)=1, norm one and the ratio identity give X=±b/c_u and Y=±a/c_u. Therefore c_u is exactly the common reduced denominator of the real and imaginary coordinates of Z_ph.
Each w_i has common coordinate denominator D_i=R/h_i. Hence c_u divides D_1D_2D_3=R³/H_content. In the K=1 packet (h_1,h_2,h_3)=(1,1,h), c_u|R³/h and c_u<=B³/h. This is a height bound for the physical product phase; it does not identify c_u with R.


2. Four-core valuation bridge
Use the retained ROUTE §17 conventions: r_i=kappa_i q_i², q_i=G_i/conjugate(G_i), Q=q_0 q_1 q_2 q_3. Here kappa_i=conjugate(epsilon_i)*conjugate(beta_i), beta_i=B_i/conjugate(B_i), N(B_i)=c_i. The kappas are rational Gaussian norm-one coefficients; they are units at both primes above every fresh p outside content, but need not be Gaussian integer units globally. Thus
Z_ph=Q³/(r_1 r_2 r_3)=q_0³ q_1 q_2 q_3/(kappa_1 kappa_2 kappa_3).
Let T_0=tau_0^sharp be the all-same core norm with the content-supported primes removed, and M=M_rel=tau_1^sharp tau_2^sharp tau_3^sharp. The four sharp norms are pairwise coprime on the retained odd split fresh support.
At p^alpha||T_0, the two Gaussian prime valuations of q_0³ are +3alpha,-3alpha. Since p is odd split and outside content, the common rational coordinate denominator has depth exactly 3alpha. At p^lambda||M, the single relative factor q_i has valuations +lambda,-lambda, so the denominator depth is exactly lambda. The other factors are units at that p. There is no fresh cancellation between four coprime cores.
Consequently c_u^sharp=T_0³ M. Since all primes of R outside content occur in these four cores and c_u|R³/H_content, every remaining prime of c_u is content-supported. Therefore the183 cofactor is
c_*=c_u/M=T_0³ w_H,
rad(w_H)|H_content, gcd(w_H,T_0 M)=1, gcd(T_0,M)=1.
For K=1, H_content=h. This exact bridge constrains the same physical c_*; it is stronger than the previous bare divisibility M|c_u. It is not an independent density factor.
Keep134: Q_S=M², C_u=1, M_G=1, Den(S)=M² t_* with gcd(t_*,M)=1. Fresh amplified C_u, interior characters and G-tail remain physical EMPTY under134. The new bridge does not reopen them.


3. Scoped summed cubic-divisor tail bound
Let E(Z,D;C) be K=1 primitive positive endpoints with R<=B, h<=C, finite nonzero u, c_u<=Z and T_0>=D, with all original orientation/content/cyclic masks, four-square tests and intrinsic R retained. For D>=1 and parameters bounded by fixed powers of B,
#E(Z,D;C) << B^o min{Z, C Z/D²}.
The first bound is183. For the second, fix h. By177, the positive integers w<=Z with rad(w)|h form B^o possibilities uniformly for h<=B^A. For each w and integer d=T_0>=D, the exact identity c_u=M d³ w allows at most floor(Z/(d³w)) positive integers M. Dropping coprimality, split-prime restrictions and physical tests here is only an upper-bound relaxation. Summing d>=D gives O(Z/(w D²)); summing content-supported w gives Z D^(-2) B^o. For every candidate c_u,183 bounds its global endpoint fiber by B^o, hence also the subset with this h. Summing h<=C proves the bound. Bounded labels are absorbed into B^o; no extra packet orientation or one-core density cost is claimed.
If one additionally requires M>=L, the region is empty whenever L D³>Z. Otherwise the bound above still applies. The B^o factors use fixed-power parameter ranges and177/183 uniformity; they are not used to manufacture a fixed-power saving.


4. Quantified obstruction on the current large-relative residual
This upper bound alone cannot certify o(M3) across the current residual. Use dyadic scales h~B^alpha, c_u<=B^z, T_0>=B^d, M>=B^m, with d>=0. The newly available upper-bound exponent is alpha+z-2d. Nonempty feasibility requires z>=m+3d, hence alpha+z-2d>=alpha+m+d>=alpha+m.
The retained180 residual gives m>=1/2-3delta_sharp/2-3alpha/2. Therefore alpha+m>=1/2-3delta_sharp/2-alpha/2. With h<=C=B^(1/6+xi), this is at least 5/12-3delta_sharp/2-xi/2. If 3delta_sharp/2+xi/2<1/12, the exponent of this available bound is strictly above1/3 before any d cost. The alternative183 bound has exponent z, likewise at least m>=1/4-3delta_sharp/2-3xi/2 uniformly, and the current surviving c_u is already >B^(1/3-delta_c); it supplies no uniform closure there.
This is an obstruction to this specific counting estimate, not a lower bound for actual endpoint occupancy and not an impossibility theorem for a stronger correlation. Cube-divisor sparsity and the h-supported integer lemma, by themselves, do not supply the missing budget. The physical four-square/full-S filters may still correlate T_0,w_H,t_* and the181 face-space data, but that correlation has not been counted.


5. Verification and scope
Exact finite-field algebra checks at p=17,29,41 verified 768 nondegenerate direction triples satisfying x_i²+y_i²=1 and sum x_i²=1: T Y=2x_1x_2x_3, S P=64(x_1x_2x_3)², P=4 S Y², and u²X²=Y² all PASS. These are algebraic test points, not positive rational physical endpoints; physical endpoint enumeration=0. The symbolic expansions and Gaussian valuations above establish the claims; finite tests do not prove asymptotic counting.
Dedup:117’s carrier tau_0³ times relative factors and its support-equivalence firewall remain in force. The present denominator is the physical product phase w_1w_2w_3, not a new independent lower-dimensional receiver.110/119 Gaussian cube image-density discussions do not authorize an additional cube-density charge.183 fixed-c_u compression remains adopted. No global counting credit is earned here.


FLAGS AND NEXT185
STATUS=PROVED_PHYSICAL_PRODUCT_PHASE_DENOMINATOR / PROVED_CUBIC_COFACTOR_BRIDGE / SCOPED_SUMMED_TAIL_BOUND / CURRENT_RESIDUAL_BUDGET_INSUFFICIENT.
NEXT_CANDIDATE=M3-T11-185: on the same K=1 large-c_u/full-S residual, seek a counted correlation between c_u=M T_0³ w_H and Den(S)=M² t_*, using actual four-square/intrinsic R and181 gcd/lcm filters. A valid route must remove or reduce the content cost or bound physical joint occupancy with a fixed-power saving. Merely summing cube divisors again, renaming occupied support, multiplying one-core densities, recharging Euclid large-k squares or E fourth-power denominators is not progress. Large-c threshold tail and K>1 low-median averaging remain separately OPEN.
STARTUP: MAIN -> INDEX -> latest184 -> only the necessary dependency sections. Full proof for this result lives only in this card. MAIN/short LEDGER/ROUTE carry summaries and references.


SOURCES
183 common-u norm-conic compression and global fixed-c_u fiber: M3-T11-183 — Global common-u hypotenuse compression and fresh-denominator-only reconciliation
177 uniform content-supported integer lemma: M3-T11-177 — Unit-median occupied-tau collapse and small-fresh sector disposal
active ROUTE §17 four-core physical phase conventions: K16-C3-M3-ROUTE-TRIVIAL-SPLIT-CYCLE

182 global fixed-u fiber;180 residual;181 face-space bridge/firewall are retained through183 and current INDEX.

﻿M3-T11-183 — Global common-u hypotenuse compression and fresh-denominator-only reconciliation
Status: NEW SCOPED GLOBAL ENDPOINT COUNT / CORRECTION OF CURRENT NEXT-ATTACK SCOPE
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; primary gate OPEN; TI parked;120 retracted;147–149 frozen.
Authority: fresh MAIN/INDEX/short LEDGER/active ROUTE/latest182. Targeted dependencies133,134,180–182. No full-history reread. Within-session deductive review; independent hostile audit NOT RUN.


1. Correct the live population before counting
133 already proves that an actual primitive positive endpoint on the finite nonzero-u branch has
u=a_u/b_u reduced, b_u>0,
N_u=a_u^2+b_u^2=c_u^2, c_u a positive integer.
This is retained, not a new183 discovery. The common parameter u is the corrected u=P*S/(S*E+P), not the retracted u/S inverse.


134 already proves, at every odd split fresh relative p^lambda||m_i outside content, that
c_p=0, v_p(Den S)=2lambda, v_p(N_u)=2lambda.
Hence exactly
Q_S=M_rel^2, C_u=1, M_G=1,
c_u=M_rel*c_*, Den(S)=M_rel^2*t_*,
gcd(c_*t_*,M_rel)=1.
All fresh interior and amplified-Gaussian branches are physically empty on this exact packet.134's argument is an original-space-triangle denominator argument, not a character-density claim:
d_i=(S-v_i)/2=2*x_i*y_i has Den(d_i)=D_i^2,
D_i=R/h_i=tau*c_i.
Freshness makes v_p(D_i)=lambda for all three directions. The targeted v_i is a p-unit, so S-v_i has its required pole2lambda only if S does too. The040 allocation law then forces c_p=0.
Scope: finite nonzero u; odd split fresh relative support; full original equal-tau/content/orientation masks. No blanket exclusion at content-supported primes or2, and no new u=infinity theorem.


The180–182 NEXT-attack wording incorrectly revived the amplified-C_u fresh tail as a live physical branch. It is superseded here by134. Their algebraic dichotomy Q_S*C_u=M_rel^2 remains true as an enlarged necessary statement, and180/181 sector estimates and182 fixed fibers remain retained. No global-credit flag changes. Fresh Gaussian tail must not be resumed unless134's physical denominator or targeted-unit input is invalidated.


2. New global fixed-c_u fiber from133 plus182
182 proves, uniformly over realized finite nonzero u and over all content/coefficient packets, that the exact primitive physical endpoint fiber is <=B^o(1) for R<=B. Its polynomial-height and normalized-reconstruction assumptions are retained here.


Fix c_u=C. Then (a_u,b_u) is a primitive integer point on
a_u^2+b_u^2=C^2,
with a_u!=0,b_u>0,gcd(a_u,b_u)=1.
There are at most4*tau(C^2) integral ordered representations: in Z[i], a_u+i*b_u has norm C^2; equivalently the standard sum-of-two-squares representation bound r_2(C^2)<=4*tau(C^2) applies. This elementary bound may include nonprimitive points, which is harmless for the upper bound. Signs and swapped legs change only a bounded constant.
Because every realized C is B^O(1), tau(C^2)=B^o(1) uniformly. For each resulting rational u, use182's global fiber. Allocate half of any epsilon to representation count and half to endpoint fiber.


Therefore the new content-free physical statement is
m_c(C;B):=# {primitive positive endpoints R<=B with c_u=C} <= B^o(1),
uniformly over all realized C and without a moving-content multiplier.
This is a composition theorem.133's norm-square result and182's fixed-u result individually do not state this fixed-hypotenuse endpoint fiber.


3. New summed small-hypotenuse and small-u-height sectors
For any Z in the physical polynomial-height window,
#E_{c_u<=Z}(B) <= Z*B^o(1).
One may also count rational u directly: every primitive positive Pythagorean pair has
{abs(a_u),b_u}={m^2-n^2,2mn}, c_u=m^2+n^2,
with m>n>0 coprime and opposite parity. The number of such m,n with m^2+n^2<=Z is O(Z), with a bounded sign/leg allowance. Summing182 over these labels gives the same Z*B^o(1). This is an upper bound on an exact physical sector, not a claim that arbitrary conic labels are physical endpoints.


Use a fixed delta_c>0 and take
Z=B^(1/3-delta_c).
Then
#E_{c_u<=Z}(B) <= B^(1/3-delta_c+o(1))=o(M3)
under the retained M3 comparison scale. Choose the B^o envelope with exponent below delta_c; do not replace the required fixed-power margin by bare little-o support.


For H(u)=max(abs(a_u),b_u),
H(u)<=c_u<=sqrt(2)*H(u).
Consequently
#E_{H(u)<=T}(B) <= T*B^o(1),
and
#E_{N_u<=X}(B) <= sqrt(X)*B^o(1).
Thus the small-u-height disposal threshold improves from182's unrestricted rational-label T^2 bound at T=B^(1/6-epsilon) to T=B^(1/3-epsilon) on the actual norm-square physical population. Equivalently one can dispose of N_u<=B^(2/3-2epsilon).
This scoped result applies over all content packets on the finite nonzero-u locus, including the relevant K=1 residual. It does not settle any remaining projective or other population branch.


4. Corrected current residual and sufficient next theorem
Intersect the new retained sector complement with180–181:
K=1, h<=B^(1/6+xi),
Sigma_sharp>B^(1/3-delta_sharp),
M_rel>B^(1/4-3delta_sharp/2-3xi/2),
c_u>B^(1/3-delta_c).
By134, the fresh conductor lies wholly in Den(S):
Q_S=M_rel^2, C_u=1,
Den(S)>=M_rel^2>B^(1/2-3delta_sharp-3xi).
Also c_u=M_rel*c_* and Den(S)=M_rel^2*t_* with the exact fresh coprimality above. These are retained pointwise constraints, not two independent density savings.


The remaining hard problem is a same-physical-measure count of occupied large-c_u / full-S-denominator states under the four half-angle square tests and intrinsic height
R=lcm_i sqrt(Den((S-v_i)/2))<=B,
with original Gaussian/coefficient/cyclic masks,181 face-space gcd/lcm bridge and unit-denominator coprimality. Do not replace this physical height by c_u, by a rational box, or by a bare Heron cover.135's x=-1/8 physical emptiness and147–149 freezes remain retained.


A sufficient scoped theorem is an actual upper bound
# {the exact above residual endpoints} << B^(1/3-eta)
for a fixed eta>0, after choosing fixed sector margins. It must sum moving content and the complementary c_*,t_* occupancy; fixed fibers alone do not prove it.
Occupied c_u support is power-equivalent to endpoint count on this finite-u population by section2. This equivalence is a firewall: large-c_u support is not automatically a smaller gate merely because its labels are integral. The new result is the proved small-c_u endpoint sector, not an unproved large-support gain.


5. Deduplication, verification and limits
INDEX search identified133's norm square and134's fresh-G emptiness before promotion. They are explicitly dependencies, not new research credit.
Elementary exact replay checked all51 unordered primitive positive Pythagorean pairs with c_u<=320: Euclid inverse, opposite parity, gcd and a_u^2+b_u^2=c_u^2 all PASS. Maximum2 such pairs shared one c_u in that finite check. This verifies the counting interface only. Physical endpoints enumerated=0; the proof of the asymptotic bound is the divisor/Euclid argument plus182's retained uniform fiber, not this finite replay.
Independent hostile audit NOT RUN. If182's uniform global physical fiber or133/134's physical lift is invalidated, the corresponding183 conclusions must be re-audited. No new theorem about ranks or number fields is imported.


Flags
M3_T11_FIXED_COMMON_U_HYPOTENUSE_GLOBAL_PHYSICAL_MULTIPLICITY=BO1
M3_T11_SMALL_COMMON_U_HYPOTENUSE_GLOBAL_ENDPOINT_SECTOR=true
M3_T11_SMALL_U_HEIGHT_GLOBAL_BOUND=T_BO1
M3_T11_FRESH_GAUSSIAN_TAIL_PHYSICAL_EMPTY_RETAINED_FROM_134=true
M3_T11_CURRENT_EXTREME_ATTACK_DENOMINATOR_ONLY=true
M3_T11_LARGE_COMMON_U_HYPOTENUSE_OCCUPANCY_DEFICIT_PROVED=false
M3_T11_183_INDEPENDENT_HOSTILE_AUDIT=NOT_RUN
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0


Next184
Start from183 then182 and134, using INDEX to fetch only necessary dependencies. Attack the full-S-denominator large-c_u residual with an actual summed count or a genuinely new constraint coupling c_*,t_* to181's physical filters. Preserve four-square/intrinsic-R reconstruction. Do not revive an amplified fresh C_u branch, interior local characters or an independent E fourth-power density. Large-c threshold tail andK>1 low-median averaging remain separate OPEN branches.

﻿M3-T11-182 — Content-free anti-root and symmetric endpoint fibers
Status: DEDUCTIVE PROMOTION USING RETAINED UNIFORM TORSION THEOREMS / GLOBAL COUNTING GATE OPEN
Authority: Drive current MAIN/INDEX/short RESULT-LEDGER, latest 181; active ROUTE §§24,30,35,42–43; primitive physical normalization in174. No restart of archived history. This card removes the content/coefficient-packet restriction from fixed-parameter physical fibers; it does not prove a moving-support deficit. No independent external hostile audit has been performed for182.


1. Exact measure and notation
Count primitive positive physical cuboid endpoints of height R<=B, with rational norm-one torus variables from the full retained triple-spin/double-lift. Include all physical denominator, coprimality, positivity and canonical-order masks. Passing to a larger algebraic fiber is used only for an upper bound; no ambient density is transferred to the endpoint measure.
Retain kappa_i=conj(epsilon_i)*conj(beta_i), q_i=G_i/conj(G_i), r_i=kappa_i*q_i^2, Q=q0*q1*q2*q3, with norm one. Set
s=r2/r1, t=r3/r1, C=q0^2*q1^2/(kappa2*kappa3).
The full sphere equation is
F(C,s,t)=C^2*s^2*t^2+(1+C^2)*(s^2+t^2)+2*C*s*t+1=0.
The corrected distinguished anti-root z3=i*v3 satisfies
v3^2=Lambda(C)*Lambda(s)*Lambda(C*s), Lambda(a)=a+a^(-1).
The cyclic v1,v2 are those of ROUTE §35. S=sum(v_i), E=sum_{i<j}(v_i*v_j), P=product(v_i), and finite u=P*S/(S*E+P). Avoid the retracted rational-z and common-v claims.


2. Content-free physical reconstruction — new bridge
Put y=Q/r1. Direct cancellation gives
y^2=C*s*t.
The normalized physical edge vector is
(e1/R,e2/R,e3/R)=(Re(y),Re(y/s),Re(y/t)).
Thus (C,s,t), together with at most two rational Gaussian square roots y of C*s*t, determines the normalized physical vector independently of every content/coefficient packet.
For norm-one y,s,t, put x1=(y+y^(-1))/2, x2=(y/s+s/y)/2, x3=(y/t+t/y)/2. The exact Laurent identity is
F(C,s,t)=4*y^2*(x1^2+x2^2+x3^2-1), when y^2=C*s*t.
Indeed 4*sum(x_i^2)-4 = y^2*(1+s^(-2)+t^(-2))+y^(-2)*(1+s^2+t^2)+2; multiplying by y^2=C*s*t gives precisely F.
A fixed rational normalized vector has at most one primitive positive integral edge vector. Clear its three rational denominators and divide the integer edge vector by its gcd. Any second integral vector on the same ray is a positive integer multiple of this primitive vector. The required integral R and face diagonals then either exist uniquely or reject it. Permutations/sign charts contribute only an absolute bounded factor. No outer sum over h or over coefficient packets remains at this reconstruction step.


3. Fixed nonzero anti-root has a global B^o fiber
Fix v=v3 in Q, v!=0. Let x=Lambda(C), z=Lambda(s), w=Lambda(C*s), X=x^2, Y=z^2. ROUTE §30 gives
X*Y*(X+Y-v^2-4)+v^4=0.
For a rational nonzero v this is smooth genus one: the only singular conditions are v^2 in {0,-1,8}, none possible here. The rational flexes at infinity give the retained rational 3-torsion.
The previously retained uniform bounded-height torsion theorem counts B^o(1) rational (X,Y) on this same cubic. Its coefficients depend only on v, not on a content packet. All physical torus, trace, cubic-point and parameter heights are uniformly B^O(1) even while packets vary: their defining Gaussian coordinates/content factors are bounded by polynomial powers of R<=B, and every rational operation here has fixed degree. The exponent constants do not depend on the packet. This is the sole uniform-theorem input; it is the already retained §30/§43 input, not a new rank or genus assertion.
For each (X,Y), choose x,z in Q with squares X,Y (at most four sign pairs), and solve
C^2-x*C+1=0, s^2-z*s+1=0
in Q(i) (at most four pairs). Then t satisfies
(1+C^2+C^2*s^2)*t^2+2*C*s*t+(1+s^2+C^2*s^2)=0.
It is never identically zero because 2*C*s!=0; even when the quadratic coefficient vanishes there is at most one t. Hence at most two t values. Finally y^2=C*s*t contributes at most two y, and section2 gives a unique primitive physical vector. Explicit inverse bound <=64 per cubic point, before a bounded chart/permutation allowance. Missing roots, bad norm, wrong anti-root orientation or failed physical filters simply remove candidates.
Therefore, uniformly over realized v!=0,
# {all primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B with v3=v} <= B^o(1),
with NO fixed content/coefficient-packet assumption.
Zero trace gives a zero physical edge on F, so v_i=0 is excluded on the retained positive endpoint locus. For example Lambda(C)=0 gives F=-(s*t-C)^2 and y^2=-1, hence x1=0; the cyclic trace-zero cases similarly kill another edge.


4. Global fixed-S and fixed-u fibers
On the retained nondegenerate finite-u locus (S!=0,u!=0), use the canonical §43 uniform fixed-field 3-torsion estimates. They count B^o(1) bounded-height symmetric quartic points, not content labels, since their curve equations depend only on the fixed S or u. Their polynomial-height adapter remains uniform as in section3.
For fixed u, the quartic gives B^o choices of S; for fixed S it gives B^o choices of u. The quartic discriminants are respectively
-65536*u^2*(1+u^2)^2*(25*u^2-2)^3,
1048576*S^2*(S^2-8)^3*(1+S^2)^6.
All realized rational nonzero parameters are smooth. Retained torsion is over the single field Q(sqrt(-3)); no new field is introduced.
For each (S,u),
P=4*u^2*S/(1+u^2),
E=(4*u*S-4*u^2)/(1+u^2).
The split cubic T^3-S*T^2+E*T-P fixes the unordered anti-root triple; there are at most six labeled triples. Each nonzero v3 has the content-free physical B^o fiber of section3. Combining two B^o bounds still gives B^o (allocate half of any epsilon to each).
Consequently
fixed realized S!=0 => global physical endpoint fiber B^o,
fixed realized finite u!=0 => global physical endpoint fiber B^o,
over all content packets, with the exact physical filters retained.
This upgrades the scope of036/§43. It does not retract their previous per-packet statements. No claim is made here for u=infinity; the current large-fresh branch M_rel>1 already excludes that branch by the retained conductor argument.


5. Valid summed sectors and explicit limits
For reduced rational height H(a/b)=max(|a|,b), the number of rational labels H<=T is O(T^2). Therefore the finite-u nondegenerate endpoint sectors
#E_{H(S)<=T} <= T^2*B^o,
#E_{H(u)<=T} <= T^2*B^o.
Taking T=B^(1/6-epsilon) makes either sector o(M3), using the retained M3 scale B^(1/3) up to logarithms. There is no outer C or C^(3/2) multiplier. These are scoped upper bounds; this card does not claim a new nonempty subpopulation of the current residual tail or charge them independently of previously consumed sectors.
Likewise any finite realized S- or u-label support has endpoint mass equal to its occupied support at power scale. This equivalence warns against presenting a support re-labeling as a new saving.


6. Relation to current182 extreme-tail attack
On the K=1 small-c residual from180–181,
Sigma_sharp>B^(1/3-delta_sharp),
M_rel>B^(1/4-3*delta_sharp/2-3*xi/2),
Q_S*C_u=M_rel^2.
The genuine gain of this card is a uniform physical multiplicity theorem across packets. The remaining task is to count occupied labels or equivalent endpoint mass on the large-Q_S denominator branch and the amplified-C_u norm branch. Fixed fibers and deterministic denominator/norm lower bounds alone give no such tail upper bound.
Keep181 gcd/lcm bridge, gcd(AB,tau)=1, two-unit denominator filters and full double lift. Never multiply one-core root-line densities; never recharge Euclid-saturated large-k squares, the019 determinant,032/033 product modulus, or E fourth-power denominator. Large Sigma_sharp support alone remains the active-tau re-labeling firewalled by181.

records.title: M3-T11-181 — Unit-median face-space gcd/lcm bridge and fresh-Sigma support-equivalence firewall
records.content:
﻿M3-T11-181 — Unit-median face-space gcd/lcm bridge and fresh-Sigma support-equivalence firewall


CARD_ID: M3-T11-181
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-181
STATUS: PROVED_K1_FACE_SPACE_GCD_LCM_BRIDGE / PROVED_K1_SMALL_SHARED_GCD_ENDPOINT_SECTOR / FRESH_SIGMA_SUPPORT_POWER_EQUIVALENT_TO_ACTIVE_TAU / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_010_163_176_177_180


1. Current authority and decision


Fresh MAIN, CARD-INDEX, current short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-180 were read first. Retained M3-T11-004/007/010/160/163/176/177 and the later symmetric-route firewalls were checked only where needed.


M3-T11-180 left two candidate continuations:
(A) count the large occupied Sigma_sharp support;
(B) attack the symmetric Q_S/C_u extreme tails.


This card proves that route (A), as a pure occupied-support problem, is power-scale equivalent to the already-open active-tau support gate. Thus it is not a genuinely narrower receiver by itself.


Separately, the exact K=1 two-unit denominator filters of M3-T11-176 collapse to a simple face/space gcd-lcm identity. This produces a new K=1 shared-divisor coordinate k, a summed small-k endpoint sector, and a precise large-k residual. The associated square-divisor condition on the primitive space triangle is Euclid-saturated and receives no independent density credit.


No global endpoint upper bound or primary-gate closure is claimed.


2. Exact K=1 face and space triangles


Relabel an exact K=1 endpoint as in M3-T11-176:
h_1=h_2=1, h_3=h,
R=h*tau.


The primitive space triangle complementary to e_3 is
u=e_3/h,
v=f_12/h,
u^2+v^2=tau^2,
gcd(u,v)=1.                                           (181.1)


For the physical face (e_1,e_2,f_12), put
g=gcd(e_1,e_2),
A=e_1/g,
B=e_2/g,
n=f_12/g.


Then
A^2+B^2=n^2,
gcd(A,B)=1,
and the triple (A,B,n) is primitive.                 (181.2)


Because the whole endpoint is primitive, one has
gcd(h,g)=1.                                          (181.3)


Indeed, any prime dividing both h and g divides e_3 through h and divides e_1,e_2 through g, contradicting gcd(e_1,e_2,e_3)=1.


The same physical diagonal satisfies
f_12=g*n=h*v.                                        (181.4)


Using (181.3), h divides n and g divides v. Define
k=n/h=v/g.                                           (181.5)


Therefore exactly
n=h*k,
v=g*k,
gcd(h,g)=1.                                          (181.6)


It follows immediately that
k=gcd(n,v),                                          (181.7)
h=n/gcd(n,v),                                        (181.8)
g=v/gcd(n,v),                                        (181.9)
and
f_12=lcm(n,v).                                       (181.10)


These identities are on the exact physical endpoint measure.


3. Re-expression of the M3-T11-176 two-unit denominator filters


In the M3-T11-176 normalized chart,
rho=v/tau,
x=A/n,
b0=B/n.


Because the two primitive triangles give
gcd(v,tau)=1,
gcd(A,n)=gcd(B,n)=1,
one has exactly
gcd(v*A,tau*n)=gcd(v,n)*gcd(A,tau),                  (181.11)
gcd(v*B,tau*n)=gcd(v,n)*gcd(B,tau).                  (181.12)


Hence
den(rho*x)
=tau*n/[gcd(v,n)*gcd(A,tau)],                       (181.13)
den(rho*b0)
=tau*n/[gcd(v,n)*gcd(B,tau)].                       (181.14)


The K=1 unit-content conditions
den(rho*x)=den(rho*b0)=R=h*tau                     (181.15)
are therefore equivalent to
gcd(A,tau)=gcd(B,tau)=1
and
gcd(n,v)=n/h.                                        (181.16)


Since gcd(A,B)=1, equality of the two reduced denominators cannot hide a common nontrivial gcd with tau.


Thus the denominator filters are not mysterious extra local events on the K=1 population. They are exactly the face-space gcd bridge (181.7)-(181.9) plus the coprimality
gcd(A*B,tau)=1.                                      (181.17)


Also, because k|v and gcd(v,tau)=1,
gcd(k,tau)=1.                                        (181.18)


4. Fixed-k endpoint count on the live small-c branch


Now impose the live small-c bound
1<=h<=C=B^(1/6+xi).


Fix k and h.


Then the primitive face hypotenuse
n=h*k
is fixed. The number of ordered primitive Pythagorean face directions (A,B,n) is bounded by a divisor function and hence is B^o(1).


Each such ordered direction fixes one physical rational face ratio A/B. Retained M3-T11-010 gives uniform B^o(1) multiplicity for each fixed physical edge ratio, with physical contents/lifts included. The same physical charging discipline as M3-T11-160/163 applies; all remaining endpoint conditions only remove states.


Consequently
#{K=1 exact endpoints with fixed (h,k)}
<=B^o(1).                                            (181.19)


Summing h<=C gives, uniformly for every fixed k,
#{K=1 exact endpoints with this k}
<=C*B^o(1).                                          (181.20)


Therefore for every K>=1,
P_K1,k<=K(B;C)
<=C*K*B^o(1).                                        (181.21)


Choose a fixed epsilon_k>0 with xi+epsilon_k<1/6 and put
K=B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_k).                              (181.22)


Then
P_K1,k<=K(B;C)
<=B^(1/3-epsilon_k+o(1))
=o(M3(B)).                                           (181.23)


Thus after deleting this exact endpoint sector, every surviving small-c K=1 endpoint satisfies
k=gcd(n,v)
>B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_k).                               (181.24)


This is a new scoped K=1 receiver. Quantitatively it is compatible with the retained small-primitive-face-hypotenuse deletion: n=h*k. It is not an independent multiplicative saving relative to M3-T11-161/163.


5. Large-k Euclid allocation and saturation firewall


Because the primitive face hypotenuse n is odd and h is odd, k is odd.


From the primitive space triangle,
v^2=(tau-u)(tau+u).                                  (181.25)


For every odd prime power p^a||k, one has p∤tau by (181.18). Therefore p cannot divide both tau-u and tau+u, since their gcd divides 2*tau.


Thus the p^(2a) contribution from k^2|v^2 is allocated wholly to exactly one of tau-u or tau+u.


There are unique pairwise coprime positive integers k_-,k_+ with
k_-*k_+=k,
k_-^2 | tau-u,
k_+^2 | tau+u.                                      (181.26)


Choosing the larger one gives q=max(k_-,k_+), hence
q>=sqrt(k),
q^2>=k.                                               (181.27)


On the residual (181.24),
q^2
>B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_k).                               (181.28)


Equivalently,
u == +tau mod k_-^2
or
u == -tau mod k_+^2.                                 (181.29)


However this is not a new rare square-divisor event. In every primitive Pythagorean triangle the normalized factors tau±u are themselves squares or twice squares in Euclid parameters. The large q in (181.26) is therefore a saturated Euclid-root allocation of the already-forced large shared divisor k.


No lattice-density, square-divisor-density or root-line probability may be charged from (181.26)-(181.29) without a genuinely new same-endpoint correlation theorem.


This is analogous in spirit to the retained M3-T11-167 saturation firewall, but it concerns the K=1 face-diagonal leg v and the new face/space shared gcd k, not the global edge-leg L_free router.


6. Fresh-Sigma occupied support is power-equivalent to active tau


Let S_tau^(1)(B) be the occupied K=1 tau values and S_SigmaSharp(B) the occupied K=1 Sigma_sharp values from M3-T11-180.


M3-T11-177 proves, uniformly,
#{K=1 endpoints with fixed tau}<=B^o(1).             (181.30)


M3-T11-180 proves, uniformly,
#{K=1 endpoints with fixed Sigma_sharp}<=B^o(1).     (181.31)


Build the exact endpoint incidence graph whose left vertices are occupied tau values, right vertices are occupied Sigma_sharp values, and whose edges are physical endpoints.


A fixed tau vertex is incident to at most B^o(1) endpoints by (181.30), hence to at most B^o(1) occupied Sigma_sharp values.
A fixed Sigma_sharp vertex is incident to at most B^o(1) endpoints by (181.31), hence to at most B^o(1) occupied tau values.


Therefore
|S_SigmaSharp(B)|
<=B^o(1)|S_tau^(1)(B)|,                              (181.32)
|S_tau^(1)(B)|
<=B^o(1)|S_SigmaSharp(B)|.                           (181.33)


So the two supports have the same polynomial exponent.


Together with the fixed-fiber theorems,
#E_K1(B),
|S_tau^(1)(B)|,
|S_SigmaSharp(B)|
are all power-equivalent.                            (181.34)


Consequently, after the useful small-Sigma_sharp sector deletion of M3-T11-180, a bare theorem that only counts the remaining occupied Sigma_sharp support is not a new narrower theorem species: at power scale it is the original active-tau support gate in another coordinate.


A genuinely new continuation through Sigma_sharp would need additional structure on the LARGE support, not merely a change of support label.


7. Operational consequence for the current route


Route (A) from M3-T11-180 is now firewalled:


LargeFreshSigmaSupport alone
= active-tau support at power scale.                 (181.35)


The exact small-Sigma_sharp sector theorem remains retained and useful; only the idea that the remaining large support is automatically simpler is rejected.


The new k-coordinate also does not by itself solve the residual:
- small k is disposed by (181.23);
- large k yields the exact face-space gcd/lcm structure and saturated Euclid allocation;
- no independent density saving follows from q^2|tau±u.


Therefore the preferred genuinely non-redundant continuation is M3-T11-180 route (B):
the symmetric extreme allocation
Q_S*C_u=M_rel^2,
with large Q_S denominator support versus large C_u amplified common-u Gaussian norm, preserving the exact physical measure.


The retained two large relative M3-T11-026 moduli from179 and the new k bridge may be used only if a future theorem couples them to the symmetric extreme allocation on the SAME endpoint.


8. Novelty and limits


CARD-INDEX searches for:
- Sigma_sharp active tau support;
- fresh Sigma support equivalent;
- occupied fresh Sigma tau;
- face space lcm bridge;
- shared face space gcd;
- K1 denominator gcd lcm;
- n/gcd(n,v);
- tau±u face-diagonal square-divisor
found no prior card stating (181.5)-(181.18), the fixed-k sector (181.21)-(181.24), or the support-equivalence firewall (181.32)-(181.35).


M3-T11-163 already controls small primitive face legs globally; M3-T11-161 controls small primitive face hypotenuse. The present small-k sector is not credited independently from those global geometric sectors when they overlap.


No physical endpoint was enumerated. No independent hostile audit is claimed. No global endpoint bound, primary-gate closure or P/M3 theorem is proved.


NEW_K1_FACE_SPACE_GCD_LCM_BRIDGE=true
NEW_K1_DENOMINATOR_FILTER_EXACT_GCD_FORM=true
NEW_K1_SMALL_SHARED_GCD_ENDPOINT_SECTOR=true
K1_LARGE_SHARED_GCD_EUCLID_SATURATED=true
K1_FRESH_SIGMA_SUPPORT_POWER_EQUIVALENT_ACTIVE_TAU=true
LARGE_FRESH_SIGMA_SUPPORT_STANDALONE_NOVELTY=false
NEW_GLOBAL_ENDPOINT_BOUND=false
PRIMARY_GATE_CLOSED=false
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0


9. Drive-only handoff


LATEST_RESEARCH_CARD=M3-T11-181
NEXT_CANDIDATE=M3-T11-182
CURRENT_ATTACK=SymmetricExtremeTailWithK1PhysicalFilters


182 should NOT spend another card merely recounting occupied Sigma_sharp values or treating large k as a square-divisor density event.


Primary continuation:
use the M3-T11-180 residual
Sigma_sharp>B^(1/3-delta_sharp),
M_rel>B^(1/4-(3/2)delta_sharp-(3/2)xi),
together with the exact symmetric partition
Q_S*C_u=M_rel^2.


Attack either:
(A) large Q_S denominator support on exact K=1 endpoints; or
(B) large C_u amplified common-u norm support.


Retain:
- M3-T11-036 fixed-S/fixed-u B^o(1) physical fibers;
- M3-T11-039/040 conductor partition;
- M3-T11-042-A E fourth-power denominator only as a marker;
- M3-T11-176 exact denominator filters, now equivalently (181.16)-(181.18);
- the exact face-space bridge n=h*k, v=g*k, f_12=lcm(n,v);
- large Sigma / large D_min;
- full triple-spin and torus double-lift selectors.


Do not multiply:
- Q_S and C_u savings;
- the two M3-T11-026 moduli;
- the k Euclid-square allocation;
- M3-T11-019 determinant;
- M3-T11-032/033 product modulus;
- M_rel^4|Den(E).


The separate threshold-specific large-c branch remains OPEN. K>1 low-median averaging remains OPEN. TI parked, 120 retracted, 147-149 frozen.

records.title: M3-T11-180 — Dual-fresh Plucker common-coordinate CRT and content-supported norm quotient
records.content:
﻿M3-T11-180 — Dual-fresh Plucker common-coordinate CRT and content-supported norm quotient


CARD_ID: M3-T11-180
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-180
STATUS: PROVED_K1_DUAL_FRESH_PLUCKER_COMMON_COORDINATE / PROVED_CONTENT_SUPPORTED_PLUCKER_NORM_QUOTIENT / ROOTLINE_DENSITY_FIREWALL / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_015_018_019_026_029_030_033_176_177_179


1. Current authority and decision


Fresh MAIN, CARD-INDEX, current short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-179 were read first. Retained M3-T11-015/018/019/023/024/026/029/030/032/033/176/177 were checked only where needed.


Work on the exact K=1 residual of M3-T11-179:
c_max<=C=B^(1/6+xi),
h_middle=1,
m_(1)m_(2)>B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_2),
with large Sigma, large D_min, full Gaussian orientation, triple-spin, torus double-lift, M3-T11-176 denominator filters and all physical endpoint masks retained.


Let a,b be the deterministic labels of the two largest fresh relative cores, so
m_a,m_b are distinct relative fresh norms,
M_ab:=m_a*m_b,
and
M_ab^2>B^(1/3-2xi-2epsilon_2).                      (180.1)


The new result is that the two large fresh cores can be combined LEGALLY on one pre-existing physical coordinate from the M3-T11-019 Plucker factor pair. This does not identify the distinct anti-roots of M3-T11-029 and does not use the withdrawn common-v CRT.


Moreover, after the full dual fresh modulus is removed from the primitive Plucker norm, the remaining integer cofactor has rational-prime support contained in 2h. Thus the dual-large fresh residual is routed to one common-coordinate primitive Gaussian root line with content-supported norm quotient.


No independent root-line density saving is claimed.


2. Torus homogenization and exact fresh valuation in H_i


Use the retained M3-T11-018/019 homogenization
t_i=y_i/x_i,
gcd(x_i,y_i)=1,
H_i=x_i^2+y_i^2,
r_i=(x_i+i*y_i)^2/H_i=(x_i+i*y_i)/(x_i-i*y_i).     (180.2)


Retained M3-T11-015 gives, up to bounded unit/parity normalization,
r_i=
conj(epsilon_i)*conj(B_i/conj(B_i))*q_i^2,
q_i=G_i/conj(G_i),                                  (180.3)
with N(B_i)=c_i and N(G_i)=tau_i.


On K=1, after deterministic relabeling,
(c_1,c_2,c_3)=(h,h,1)
up to bounded permutation, so every odd prime in the coefficient packet divides h.


Let p^alpha||m_i=tau_i^sharp. By definition p is an odd split prime outside the content support. Choose the oriented Gaussian prime pi over p occurring in G_i^sharp. In (180.3) the pi-adic valuation of r_i is exactly 2alpha: the coefficient packet is a p-unit and G_i^2 contributes pi^(2alpha), while the conjugate orientation contributes none.


Because (x_i,y_i) is primitive, writing P_i=x_i+i*y_i gives
r_i=P_i/conj(P_i),
and min(v_pi(P_i),v_conj(pi)(P_i))=0.
Therefore
v_pi(P_i)=2alpha,
v_conj(pi)(P_i)=0,
so
v_p(H_i)=2alpha.                                    (180.4)


Hence exactly on the fresh support,
m_i^2 | H_i,
and if
K_i:=H_i/m_i^2,                                     (180.5)
then every odd prime divisor of K_i lies in the content support. Safely including the bounded 2-adic normalization,
rad(K_i)|2h.                                         (180.6)


This is stronger than merely saying the determinant 2H_i of M3-T11-019 is large: it identifies the entire nonfresh quotient of H_i on K=1.


3. The shared Plucker factor pair


For the selected pair a,b define the exact M3-T11-019 quantities
A_ab=x_a*x_b+y_a*y_b,
B_ab=y_a*x_b-x_a*y_b,
F_ab^+=A_ab+B_ab,
F_ab^-=A_ab-B_ab.                                   (180.7)


The standard dot/cross identity gives
A_ab^2+B_ab^2=H_a*H_b,
hence
(F_ab^+)^2+(F_ab^-)^2
=2H_aH_b.                                           (180.8)


This pair is one of the actual six bilinear factors in the retained triple-spin square cover. It is not an auxiliary ambient coordinate.


4. Each large fresh core acts on the same factor ratio


For m_a, equation (180.4) gives an oriented square root omega_a modulo m_a^2 such that
y_a == omega_a*x_a mod m_a^2,
omega_a^2 == -1 mod m_a^2.                          (180.9)


Because x_a is an m_a-unit, direct substitution into (180.7) yields
F_ab^+ == omega_a*F_ab^- mod m_a^2.                 (180.10)


Similarly, for the b-core there is omega_b^2==-1 mod m_b^2 with
y_b == omega_b*x_b mod m_b^2.
Now the antisymmetry of B_ab reverses the orientation, giving
F_ab^+ == -omega_b*F_ab^- mod m_b^2.                (180.11)


These are congruences on the SAME rational coordinate F_ab^+/F_ab^-.


They are not the distinct anti-root coordinates v_a,v_b of M3-T11-029. Thus combining (180.10)-(180.11) by CRT is legal.


5. Primitivity at both fresh moduli


Let p be an odd prime dividing m_a. Suppose p divided both F_ab^+ and F_ab^-.
Then p divides A_ab and B_ab.


But
A_ab+i*B_ab
=(x_a+i*y_a)*(x_b-i*y_b).                           (180.12)


At p, the first factor contains exactly one Gaussian orientation above p by (180.4), while p does not divide H_b because the relative fresh supports are pairwise coprime and p is outside the content support. Hence the second factor is a unit at both primes over p.


Therefore the product in (180.12) cannot be divisible by the rational prime p, which would require both Gaussian orientations. Contradiction.


Thus
gcd(F_ab^-,m_a)=gcd(F_ab^+,m_a)=1,
and cyclically the same holds for m_b. In particular,
gcd(F_ab^-,M_ab)=1.                                 (180.13)


Let
g_ab=gcd(F_ab^+,F_ab^-),
X_ab=F_ab^+/g_ab,
Y_ab=F_ab^-/g_ab.                                   (180.14)


Then
gcd(X_ab,Y_ab)=1,
gcd(g_ab,M_ab)=1,
gcd(Y_ab,M_ab)=1.                                   (180.15)


6. Legal dual-core CRT on one primitive coordinate


Since gcd(m_a,m_b)=1, CRT gives a unique class rho_ab modulo M_ab^2 satisfying
rho_ab == omega_a mod m_a^2,
rho_ab == -omega_b mod m_b^2.                       (180.16)


Both local classes square to -1, hence
rho_ab^2 == -1 mod M_ab^2.                          (180.17)


After reduction by g_ab, equations (180.10)-(180.11) become the primitive common root line
X_ab == rho_ab*Y_ab mod M_ab^2,
gcd(Y_ab,M_ab)=1.                                   (180.18)


Therefore
M_ab^2 | X_ab^2+Y_ab^2.                             (180.19)


By (180.1), the common rational modulus satisfies the explicit K=1 residual lower bound
M_ab^2
>B^(1/3-2xi-2epsilon_2).                            (180.20)


This is the first legal single-coordinate CRT combination of the TWO guaranteed large fresh cores from M3-T11-179.


7. Content-supported primitive norm quotient


From (180.8) and (180.14),
X_ab^2+Y_ab^2
=
2H_aH_b/g_ab^2.                                     (180.21)


Any odd prime p not dividing h that divides g_ab would divide both A_ab and B_ab. By the same Gaussian-orientation argument as in Section 5, such a p cannot lie in exactly one of H_a,H_b; and outside h the two relative fresh supports are disjoint. Hence
rad(g_ab)|2h.                                       (180.22)


Combining (180.5)-(180.6), (180.19), (180.21) and (180.22), define
K_ab:=(X_ab^2+Y_ab^2)/M_ab^2.                       (180.23)


Then K_ab is a positive integer and
rad(K_ab)|2h.                                       (180.24)


Thus the complete fresh dual modulus has been peeled off the primitive Plucker norm; the residual norm cofactor is content-supported only.


For fixed h<=C, the support-restricted integer lemma of M3-T11-177 implies that the possible K_ab of polynomial physical height form a B^o(1) set. Therefore for fixed (h,M_ab), the possible primitive Plucker ratios
z_ab:=X_ab/Y_ab                                     (180.25)
